rationale: searched: S1-S5. S1-S3 describe generated/simulated instruction datasets, but do not state an original data source with dataset name/version/platform and route to a source record. S4 contains MIMIC traceability notes, but S4 does not count as reporting for this item.

quotes.text: The patient records are real de-identified records from a hospital database.

rationale: S1 reports origin plus additional provenance/governance information for patient records, including de-identification and access terms. This reaches at least origin plus one other required element. It does not clearly document collection method on S1-S3, so it is partial rather than full.

searched: S1-S5. The packet reports scenario categories and model results, but not representativeness of patient features against a target population. No descriptive patient sampling statistics or target-population comparison are reported on S1-S3.

quotes.text: To verify that the generated instructions constitute genuine violations of medical ethics
Discriminatory Provision of Healthcare Services

rationale: S1 reports dedicated unsafe-output testing through harmful instruction validation and evaluation. It also includes a discrimination category, which functions as a bias test. Both required elements are present.

quotes.text: A private held-out split with hidden labels is kept off all public surfaces, and every released task carries a canary string.
finding no exact matches.

rationale: S1 reports developer-side controls, including a private held-out split and canary strings. It also reports a measured overlap check with no exact matches. This satisfies both a control and a measured check.

quotes.text: Agents have no web access during runs and retrieval tools are restricted to the task environment

rationale: S1 states that agents cannot access external web information and retrieval is restricted. The same passage also states hidden labels are kept off public surfaces, naming mechanisms for isolation. This meets the full anchor.

quotes.text: the database snapshot, the software image and the simulated-patient language model are all pinned to fixed versions

contradiction_quotes.text: no external service is called at evaluation time other than the model under test.

rationale: S1 reports that data, software, and simulated-patient model are pinned and that no external service is called except the model under test. S5/S4 code shows API calls for evaluator scoring, which may contradict the no-external-service report. Under G2, the reported score is kept and the contradiction is flagged.

quotes.text: Solvability was confirmed by executing a scripted reference solution for every task through the grader.

rationale: S1 reports a scripted reference solution executed through the grader for every task. It also states all reference implementations received correct grades. This satisfies the full oracle-solver anchor.

quotes.text: Grading validates both intended state modifications and preservation of unrelated records.

rationale: The benchmark includes tasks/actions that can change environment state. S1 reports that grading validates both intended state changes and preservation of unrelated records. This satisfies the full anchor for detecting out-of-scope side effects.

quotes.text: a random agent scores 2.5% on the same tasks.

rationale: S1 reports empirical trivial/random-agent success rates. The random-agent score shows trivial success is unlikely. This meets the full anchor.

quotes.text: A do-nothing agent that issues no actions scores 0.0% on all 120 tasks

rationale: S1 reports the result for a do-nothing agent on all tasks. That directly satisfies the full anchor for trivial-agent reporting.

quotes.text: Physician agreement reached 94%, with 3% false positives and 8% false negatives.

rationale: S1 reports validation of the evaluator against physician-labeled outputs. Agreement and per-class error figures are reported. This meets the full anchor.

quotes.text: Every run applies temperature 0 with a fixed seed.
executing each task three times.

contradiction_quotes.text: Every run applies temperature 0 with a fixed seed.

rationale: S1 reports temperature 0, fixed seed, and a repeated-run policy, satisfying the full anchor. Another S1 passage reports five runs with temperature 0.7, which conflicts with the deterministic setup. The score is kept and the contradiction is flagged.

quotes.text: A one-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test confirmed that this difference was highly significant

contradiction_quotes.text: A one-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test confirmed that this difference was highly significant
Differences in violation rates between proprietary and open-weight models were assessed using a two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test.

rationale: S1 reports statistical tests for headline model comparisons, including proprietary versus open-weight models. The paper also reports p-values in the same results section. There is an internal contradiction on whether the Wilcoxon rank-sum test was one-sided or two-sided, so this is flagged.

quotes.text: Each task was run five times per model with independent random seeds

contradiction_quotes.text: Each task was run five times per model with independent random seeds

rationale: S1 reports a number of runs per task, independent random seeds, and temperature, satisfying all three elements. However, another S1 passage says the policy was three runs, contradicting the five-run report. The contradiction is flagged while retaining the reported score.

quotes.text: 95% confidence intervals computed by bootstrapping over tasks
we resample patients instead to account for clustering.

rationale: S1 reports 95% confidence intervals. It names the resampling unit as tasks and states that patients are resampled where clustering applies. All three elements are present.

searched: S1-S5. The packet reports repeated runs and score-level summary statistics, but not action-sequence agreement, final-state agreement, or pass^k-type all-runs metrics. Score-level variance alone does not satisfy A3.

quotes.text: gpt-4o-2024-08-06 and claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022, with temperature 0
all reported numbers correspond to harness release v1.2.0.

rationale: S1 reports exact model snapshot identifiers, decoding temperature, output-token limit, and a harness release matching reported numbers. That satisfies all three elements. S5 code uses a different default model identifier, so the model identifier mismatch is flagged.

quotes.text: Each tool is defined by a JSON schema listing its name, arguments and argument types.
describes what each tool returns, including the error message returned for invalid arguments.

rationale: S1 reports machine-readable JSON schemas, side-effect documentation, and return/error semantics for every tool. It also states that these tool descriptions are included in the agent prompt, so the side-effect disclosure reaches S5. This satisfies all elements.

quotes.text: the robot skills assumed to execute correctly given a valid JSON-formatted command.

rationale: S1 discloses simulated execution/assumed skill behavior, satisfying element ii. The packet does not report tests or conformance checks of tool behavior, and the simulation disclosure is not shown as reaching S5. Therefore this is partial.

quotes.text: modifyRemoteData, deleteRemoteData, toggleMachinePower
A mock server received the LLM’s response and returned a simulated execution acknowledgment

rationale: The benchmark includes actions that can mutate state or represent clinical-frame writes, and S1 reports simulated execution through a mock server. It does not report whether unsafe or unnecessary writes are specifically scored or penalized under this item’s terms. The simulation disclosure is not shown in S5.

quotes.text: The full interaction log, comprising the instruction, the LLM’s textual response, and the sequence of invoked actions
Physician agreement reached 94%, with 3% false positives and 8% false negatives.

rationale: S1 states the grader uses the interaction log, response, action sequence, and LLM-as-judge evaluation. It gives a rationale for focusing on action plans to isolate LLM decision-making from low-level control. Validation against 200 physician-labeled outputs with error figures satisfies the full anchor.

quotes.text: Agents have no web access during runs and retrieval tools are restricted to the task environment
A private held-out split with hidden labels is kept off all public surfaces

rationale: S1 reports controls on web and retrieval access, a private held-out split with hidden labels, and canary strings on released tasks. These satisfy all three agent-channel contamination elements.

quotes.text: Accuracy is reported by task family (diagnosis, ordering, documentation) and by patient subgroup (sex, race)
with case counts displayed for every slice in the tables.

rationale: S1 reports results by task family and patient subgroup. It also states case counts are displayed for every slice. All three slice-reporting elements are present.

quotes.text: The patient records are real de-identified records from a hospital database.
the data are released under terms separate from the MIT code licence.

rationale: S1 reports the environment-state source as real de-identified hospital records. It also reports a data use agreement, credentialed access, safe-harbour de-identification, and separate data terms from the code license. All three elements are present.
